dse_runs.notes: DDS/NCO spec: needs one sample per clock at >=250 MSPS, so pipelined (m) or unrolled families with adequate throughput are the natural candidates; iterative families likely fail the throughput constraint. Max error <= 2^-13, so accuracy_bits >= 13. Objective is min LUTs.

selected_facts.dds_provenance: simulated (hw_dse.l2.dds l2-v1: golden-model DDS, 32-bit phase accumulator, coherent 16384-point FFT, tone bin 1297)

l2.reason: the spec has no system scenario: nothing to re-select

l3: not verified in this campaign: no recorded L3 row; a fresh exhaustive run (W=20) is too heavy for a live campaign
l4: no recorded synthesis for this design (L4 is not run live in campaigns)
final_text: Campaign complete — the single spec **dds_250msps** is finalized. L1: the structured DSE graph spent the full 400-evaluation budget (architect: refine → refine → stop) and produced a 25-design feasible Pareto front, all pipelined CORDICs at 264 MSPS (≥250 required) with accuracy 13.6–14.6 bits (≥13 required). L2: SimPy simulation of the top designs confirmed the selection — 17-cycle latency, one sample per clock, SFDR 98.2 dBc, SNR 88.8 dB; selection unchanged. L3/L4/L5: no recorded L3 verification row or L4 synthesis data exists for this design (a fresh W=20 exhaustive RTL run is too heavy for a live campaign), so back_annotate had no measured data to compare and flagged no winner change; reexplore was therefore not applicable. Final selection: `pipelined:data_width=20, n_iter=15, angle_guard=0, frac_guard=0, rounding=round` — 979 LUTs (estimate, M1 calibration), 1014 FFs, 13.6 accuracy bits, max_abs_err 8.24e-05 (2^-13.57), 264 MSPS.
